content_data.project_title: Next-Generation Composite Materials Supply Chain Integration
content_data.project_description: Strategic initiative to consolidate and optimize composite materials sourcing across three continents, establishing strategic partnerships with tier-1 suppliers to reduce lead times by 40% and enhance manufacturing resilience.
content_data.timeline: 24 months with Phase 1 (months 1-8) focused on supplier evaluation and partnership agreements, Phase 2 (months 9-18) on integration and systems deployment, and Phase 3 (months 19-24) on optimization and performance validation
content_data.project_lead: Priya Chandrasekaran, VP of Global Supply Chain Operations
stakeholders: VP of Quality Assurance and Compliance
objectives: Implement real-time supply chain visibility platform across all manufacturing facilities
Consolidate composite materials suppliers from 47 to 12 strategic tier-1 partners across global operations
Generate annual cost savings of $18-22M through volume consolidation and improved terms
Reduce materials procurement lead times by minimum 40% through integrated planning systems
Establish dual-source arrangements for all mission-critical materials to mitigate geopolitical supply risks
deliverables: Executive dashboard with KPI tracking for lead times, costs, quality metrics, and supplier performance
Risk mitigation playbook addressing geopolitical, natural disaster, and capacity scenarios
Strategic partnership agreements with 12 tier-1 composite materials suppliers
content_data.risk_assessment: Medium-high risk profile driven by supplier transition complexity during active production cycles, potential geopolitical trade restrictions affecting materials flow, and integration challenges across legacy ERP systems in 14 facilities. Mitigation strategies include phased supplier transitions with 6-month overlap periods, pre-negotiated alternative sourcing agreements, and dedicated integration teams at each regional hub.
